{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "Tomas stood on the last board until the woman's shape had gone into the trees, and then a while longer, because leaving felt like a decision and he had not made one yet. The photograph had stopped being warm. It was only paper now, soft at one corner where a thumb had worked at it for years.

He turned and went back the way he had come. He counted this time, without meaning to. Forty-one planks. He was sure there had been thirty-something before, but the number had not seemed important then, and he could not swear to it.

The boy had not moved. His hands were still in his pockets, and he watched Tomas come the way one watches weather, with interest and no expectation.

"Well?" the boy said.

Tomas held out the photograph. The boy did not take it. He looked at it from where he stood, tilting his head, and something passed over his face that Tomas could not name, not recognition exactly, more the shadow of it, the place where recognition would go if it came.

"That's not me," the boy said.

"I didn't say it was."

"You were going to."

Tomas put the photograph in his coat. Behind them the river kept on, patient, and the bridge stood over it as it always had, or as it seemed always to have, the two stone posts on either bank like sentences with the middle left out.

"She said to bring it back when I'm sure," Tomas said.

The boy nodded slowly. "Then you'll be keeping it," he said, and started walking."}
